title: The Room We Left Behind
style: Slow emotional blues-soul ballad, around 72 BPM, minor-key warmth, intimate male baritone, conversational restrained verses, warm piano and electric guitar responses, brushed drums and bass gradually entering, human-feeling loose phrasing and purposeful silence, rising emotional tension in the bridge, broader final refrain without shouting, unhurried instrumental resolution and fade. Natural dynamic contrast, no crowded arrangement.
lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
Your coat is gone...
The hook is still there
I leave the hall light burning
Like someone might care
And every little sound
Makes me turn around

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the door is closed
But some nights...
My heart forgets

[Chorus]
There's a room we left behind
Where the hours never move
I can let the daylight in
But I can't make it new
I keep learning how to leave
What I never meant to lose

[Verse 2]
The rain has stopped
I open the blinds
The coffee's getting colder
But I think I'll be fine
There's a quiet kind of hope
In doing things alone

[Bridge]
Maybe love can end
Without a reason to regret
Maybe I can miss you
And still take another step

[Chorus]
There's a room we left behind
Where the hours never move
I can let the daylight in
But I can't make it new
I keep learning how to leave
What I never meant to lose

[Outro]
I'll turn the light off now...
And let the morning through
